The proscenium arch spans the top of the frame, gilded card scrolled at each corner, a tiny painted crest flaking at the apex.
A scalloped pelmet hangs across the opening, each scallop edged in gold braid, the fabric sagging slightly at the centre from age.
Heavy velvet curtains gather at each side, tied back with twisted gold cord, the folds catching the footlight glow from below.
A trough of tiny candle-stubs runs along the front edge, each flame raking warm amber light upward across the stage boards.
A control bar hangs above the action, four strings descending into the scene below, the bar itself bowed slightly under tension.
Two parallel grooves are cut into the stage floor, a painted flat slotted into them, the groove edges worn pale and smooth.
In the narrow wing gap at the left, a small painted tree-prop leans forward, just visible in the strip of shadow between flats.
A painted backcloth hangs at the rear, one bottom corner curling away from the roller, the paint cracked in a fine web.
A cloud cut-out on a bent wire slides halfway across the upper stage, the wire catching a glint from the footlights below.
A hairline seam crosses the stage boards near centre, two tiny hinges flush with the surface marking the trapdoor's edge.
A tiny prompt-box sits at the very front lip of the stage, its hinged lid propped open, the interior painted matte black.
A cloth sandbag rests against the base of a side flat, its cord tie loosely knotted, keeping the painted card perfectly upright.
Scraps of torn tissue paper hang mid-air above the stage, catching the light as they drift downward in a slow paper snowfall.
The stage boards are scuffed to bare timber along the centre path, and a chalk cross marks exactly where one flat's foot stands.
A slim lighting bar crosses above the proscenium, two small clip-lamps clamped to it, their beams angled steeply down onto the scene.
The stage-front lip shows chipped cream paint along its upper edge, the bare card beneath showing a warm brown where hands have touched it.
Three small wooden seats sit in the near foreground, slightly out of focus, their red-painted surfaces catching the spill of the footlights.
Motes of dust drift slowly through the beam of the nearest footlight candle, lit bright gold against the darker stage behind.
A second painted flat stands in its groove behind the first, its surface showing a faint fingerprint smear across the sky-blue paint.
A length of frayed cord hangs from the flies on the right side, its lower end tied off to a cleat on the wing flat.
The gilded inner edge of the proscenium arch shows worn patches where the gold card has rubbed to plain white at the corners.
A rolled spare backcloth leans against the rear wall inside the wings, its paper edge soft and slightly crushed from storage.
One footlight bulb glows slightly brighter than its neighbours, its small warm filament visible through the tissue-thin diffuser paper.
A tiny lead weight is tied to the base string of a hanging cut-out, keeping the wire taut and the shape steady above the stage.
The valance fringe along the pelmet bottom is uneven, three tassels shorter than the rest, the frayed ends catching the upward light.
